ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r8.claim: The hamza in aṭṭalaʿa is interrogative and is balanced by am; a reading drops it when linking speech, as in a poetic example that implies 'did he reach?'
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r8.anchor: والهمزة في أطلع للاستفهام، ولذلك عادلتها أم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains aṭṭalaʿa al-ghayb as climbing to a mountain's summit, or rising over a mountain pass; Jarīr's line uses the word for mountain ascent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r2.anchor: أطلع الغيب من قولهم: أطلع الجبل إذا ارتقى إلى أعلاه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r3.claim: The diction emphasizes the enormity of his claim: could he have ascended to the unique knowledge of the unseen? He could only expect the promised gift through unseen knowledge or a covenant from its Knower.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r3.anchor: والمعنى أن ما ادعى أن يؤتاه وتألى عليه لا يتوصل إليه إلا بأحد هذين الطريقين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r4.claim: Qatāda interprets the covenant as a righteous deed already performed, on which the man bases his expectation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: هل له عمل صالح قدمه فهو يرجو بذلك ما يقول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r5.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī asks whether God had promised him that He would grant him those things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r5.anchor: وعن الكلبي: هل عهد الله إليه أن يؤتيه ذلك

BURSEVI:v5p272#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p272#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p272#3/r1.claim: The interrogative has two hamzas; the root means climbing to a mountain's top or a mountain pass.
BURSEVI:v5p272#3/r1.anchor: همزته استفهام وأصله أأطلع من قولهم اطلع الجبل إذا ارتقى

BURSEVI:v5p272#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p272#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p272#3/r2.claim: The taunt asks whether he reached God's unique knowledge of the unseen or made a covenant with its Knower; only those routes could disclose future wealth and children.
BURSEVI:v5p272#3/r2.anchor: أقد بلغ من عظمة الشأن إلى أن ارتقى إلى علم الغيب

BURSEVI:v5p272#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p272#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p272#3/r3.claim: Another view takes the covenant as testimony of faith and righteous action, for which God promised reward.
BURSEVI:v5p272#3/r3.anchor: وقيل العهد كلمة الشهادة والعمل الصالح فإن وعد الله بالثواب عليهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r1.claim: The question أطلع الغيب rebuts the outrageous claim and is a fresh sentence; treating it as the second object of “tell me” is judged unlikely.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r1.anchor: رد لكلمته الشنعاء واظهار لبطلانها اثر ما اشير اليه بالتعجب منها فالجملة مستانفة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r2.claim: A reading with kasra on the initial hamza omits the interrogative hamza, whose presence is indicated by أم, as in the cited poetic question.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r2.anchor: بكسر الهمزة وحذف همزة الاستفهام لدلالة أم عليها كما في قوله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r3.claim: طلع is directly transitive, though it can take على; the image is ascent into possession of hidden knowledge, not ordinary knowing.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r3.anchor: والفعل متعد بنفسه وقد يتعدى بعلى وليس بلازم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r4.claim: The question challenges whether al-ʿĀṣī has mastered God's exclusive unseen knowledge to assert his future wealth and children.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r4.anchor: والمراد من الطلوع الظهور على وجه العلو والتملك ولذا اختير على التعبير بالعلم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r5.claim: He explains the question as asking whether the man looked into the Preserved Tablet.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن المعنى انظر في اللوح المحفوظ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r6.claim: He interprets the covenant as professing that there is no deity but God and hoping for the promised reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r6.anchor: قال لا اله إلا الله يرجو بها ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r7.claim: Qatada takes the covenant as righteous work for which God promised reward; another view understands a literal pledge from God that the claim will certainly occur.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r7.anchor: وعن قتادة العهد العمل الصالح الذي وعد الله تعالى عليه الثواب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r8.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r8.claim: The literal-covenant view is a rhetorical concession to the sinner's own wording; calling God al-Rahman invokes mercy as the supposed ground of the promised grant.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130#2/r8.anchor: ونقل هذا الكلبى وهذه مجاراة مع اللعين بحسب منطوق مقاله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p253/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p253/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p253/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas asks whether the man has looked into the Preserved Tablet to know the unseen.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p253/r7.anchor: ابن عباس: أنظر في اللوح المحفوظ؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p253/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p253/r8.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p253/r8.claim: Mujahid asks whether the man knows the unseen well enough to know if he is destined for Paradise.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p253/r8.anchor: مجاهد: أعلم علم الغيب حتى يعلم أفي الجنة هو أم لا؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254/r1.claim: Having a covenant with the Merciful means saying “There is no god but God.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254/r1.anchor: يعني قال لا إله إلا الله وقال قتادة:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254/r2.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254/r2.claim: Qatada says the covenant is a righteous deed sent ahead.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254/r3.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi takes the question to mean: did God promise him that he would enter Paradise?
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p254/r3.anchor: الكلبي: أعهد إليه أن يدخل الجنة؟

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:78/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:78/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:78/r1.claim: Revealed about al-As ibn Waʾil, who owed Khabbab money and refused payment until he disbelieved, then claimed future wealth and children after resurrection. “Have you seen?” means report; access to the unseen or a divine covenant are the only possible bases for the claim.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:78/r1.anchor: نزلت في العاص بن وائل كان لخباب عليه مال فتقاضاه

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:78/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:78/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:78/r2.claim: The covenant may mean testimony of faith and righteous action, for God’s reward-promise resembles a covenant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:78/r2.anchor: وقيل العهد كلمة الشهادة والعمل الصالح

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:78/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:78/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:78/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisāʾī read the word for children as a plural or dialect variant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:78/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «ولدا» وهو جمع ولد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p554/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p554/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p554/r3.claim: His claim would require either access to the unseen, which is beyond creatures, or a covenant with the Merciful earned through proper obedience; he has neither.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p554/r3.anchor: الذي هو غائب عن كل مخلوق

DURR-FULL:v5p535/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r4.claim: He reads the claim to have seen the unseen as God having shown the man the wealth he will receive, and a covenant with the Merciful as a good deed sent ahead.
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r4.anchor: عن قتادة رضي اله عنه في قوله: {أطلع الغيب} يقول: أطلعه الله الغيب يقول: ماله فيه

DURR-FULL:v5p535/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r5.claim: He explains the covenant as the testimony that there is no god but God, through which the claimant hopes for salvation.
DURR-FULL:v5p535/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا} قال: لا إله إلا الله يرجو بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r1.claim: The reply uses the wise rhetorical strategy of taking his words literally: did he inspect the unseen and verify the afterlife wealth he claims? The question denies and ridicules the claim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r1.anchor: وجملة { أطلع الغيب } جواب لكلامه على طريقة الأسلوب الحكيم بحمل كلامه على ظاهر عبارته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r2.claim: Iṭṭalaʿa is a strengthened form of ṭalaʿa, originally intransitive; when it means “look over,” it takes ʿalā, as illustrated by 37:54–55 and 18:18.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r2.anchor: أن فعل ( اطلع ) قاصر غير محتاج إلى التعدية ، قال تعالى : { قال هل أنتم مطلعون فاطلع فرآه في سواء الجحيم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r3.claim: Al-ghayb is a direct object, not a preposition left unspoken as some commentators assume; al-Zamakhsharī says the word depicts an audacious ascent to knowledge of the unseen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r3.anchor: فانتصب الغيب } في هذه الآية على المفعولية لا على نزع الخافض كما توهمه بعض المفسرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r4.claim: His boast could mean he saw wealth and children waiting in the afterlife, or saw his existing family accompanying him there; either requires access to the unseen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r4.anchor: أأشرف على عالم الغيب فرأى مالا وولدا معدينن له حين يأتي يوم القيامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r5.claim: Alternatively, he may claim a divine covenant guaranteeing wealth and children; the omitted object of “covenant” is inferred from the context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r5.anchor: أم عهد الله إليه بأنه معطيه ذلك فأيقن بحصوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r6.claim: “With the Merciful” spatially imagines a covenant as a written document kept with God, like written pacts placed in a secure, known location; the boycott pact against Banū Hāshim is an example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p159/r6.anchor: وهو استعارة بالكناية بتشبيه الوعد بصحيفة مكتوبة بها تعاهد وتعاقد بينه وبين الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r5.claim: The opening hamza of “aṭṭalaʿ al-ghayb” is interrogative; initial hamzat al-waṣl is omitted as unnecessary.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r5.anchor: وقوله أطلع الغيب توقيف والألف للاستفهام وحذفت ألف الوصل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r6.claim: Taking a covenant with the Merciful means faith and righteous deeds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r6.anchor: واتخاذ العهد معناه بالإيمان والأعمال الصالحة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r1.claim: One report says the man knew the unseen well enough to know whether he would be in Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية أعلم ما غاب عنه حتى يعلم أفي الجنة هو أم لا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r2.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās says he looked into the Preserved Tablet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r2.anchor: وقال في رواية أخرى أنظر في اللوح المحفوظ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r3.claim: One interpretation of a covenant is that he professed that there is no god but God and thereby hopes for mercy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r3.anchor: أحدها أم قال لا إله إلا الله فأرحمه بها قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r4.claim: Qatadah says the covenant means that he previously performed a good deed and hopes for its reward.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r4.anchor: والثاني أم قدم عملا صالحا فهو يرجوه قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r5.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r5.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib says the covenant is a promise that God would admit him to Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p261/r5.anchor: والثالث أم عهد اليه أنه يدخله الجنة قاله ابن السائب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r1.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r1.claim: Khabbab says al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il refused to pay his debt unless he disavowed Muhammad; when Khabbab refused, al-ʿAs claimed he would have wealth and children after resurrection, prompting revelation. The canonical collections transmit it through several routes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r1.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال: كنت رجلا قينا، وكان لي على العاص بن وائل دين، فأتيته أتقاضاه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r2.claim: In al-Bukhari's wording, the covenant question is glossed as asking whether he had a binding promise with God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r2.anchor: وقال: {أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا} قال: موثقا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r2.claim: The question about seeing the unseen denies that the claimant knows his afterlife fate well enough to swear he will receive wealth and children there.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r2.anchor: وقوله: {أطلع الغيب} : إنكار على هذا القائل، {لأوتين مالا وولدا} يعني: يوم القيامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r3.claim: The alternative asks whether God made him a covenant promising those gifts; al-Bukhari's related report glosses covenant as a binding pledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r3.anchor: {أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا} : أم له عند الله عهد سيؤتيه ذلك؟ وقد تقدم عند البخاري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn ʿAbbas that the covenant is the testimony that there is no god but God, by which the speaker hopes for reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: {أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا} قال: لا إله إلا الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi likewise interprets the covenant as testifying that there is no god but God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: {أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا} (11) قال: شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله

JISHUMI:v6p4604/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r10.claim: Ṭalaʿa ʿalayya means someone suddenly appeared; the root refers to what is seen or where an affair comes to.
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r10.anchor: ويقال: طلع علي فلان: هجم علي

JISHUMI:v6p4604/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r11.claim: A Prophetic saying uses ṭilāʿ al-arḍ for all the gold the earth can contain.
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r11.anchor: ومنه الحديث: لو أن طلاع الأرض ذهبا

JISHUMI:v6p4606/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r3.claim: The initial alif of aṭṭalaʿa is opened because it is interrogative, and the connecting alif is omitted.
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r3.anchor: أطلع فتحت ألفه؛ لأن ألفه ألف استفهام، وذهبت الألف للوصل

JISHUMI:v6p4610/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4610/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4610/r2.claim: The phrase about knowing the unseen condemns making claims about matters one does not know.
JISHUMI:v6p4610/r2.anchor: ويدل قوله: (أطلع الغيب) على قبح الخبر عما لا يعلمه ويخبر به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r2.claim: أطلع الغيب evokes climbing to a summit; the cited line by Jarīr witnesses مطلع for a mountain ascent, while the expression can mean mastering a matter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r2.anchor: إذا ارتقى إلى أعلاه وطلع الثنية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r3.claim: His claim to future wealth and children requires either knowledge of the unseen or a covenant from its Knower, and the verse asks which he possesses.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r5.claim: The covenant may mean the testimony of faith; Qatāda asks whether he has a righteous deed to rely on, while al-Kalbī asks whether God promised him the wealth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r5.anchor: في العهد : كلمة الشهادة . وعن قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r6.claim: The question about knowing the unseen may concern knowing God will grant him wealth despite disbelief, or knowing God already granted it despite disbelief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r6.anchor: معناه أعلم الغيب أنه سيؤتيه على كفره مالا وولدا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r7.claim: A covenant with the All-Merciful may mean a good deed he sent ahead.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r7.anchor: يعني عملا صالحا قدمه , قاله قتادة . الثاني

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r8.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r8.claim: Alternatively, it is a statement God promised him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r8.anchor: قولا عهد به الله إليه , حكاه ابن عيسى

MUQATIL:19:77-78/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r5.claim: The question asks whether al-ʿĀṣ had knowledge of the unseen when he claimed he would receive believers’ afterlife rewards.
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r5.anchor: يعني العاص، حين يقول: إنه يعطى في الآخرة ما يعطى المؤمنون

MUQATIL:19:77-78/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r6.claim: Having a covenant with the Merciful means believing in divine oneness.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r1.claim: اطلع comes from ascending a mountain; the interrogative hamza with elided hamzat al-wasl asks whether he looked into the Preserved Tablet and saw his destiny.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r1.anchor: من قولهم اطلع الجبل إذا ارتقى إلى أعلاه الهمزة للاستفهام وهمزة الوصل محذوفة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r2.claim: The alleged covenant may be a guarantee that he will receive wealth and children, or the testimony of faith.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r2.anchor: موثقا ان يؤتيه ذلك أو العهد كلمة الشهادة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r3.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r3.claim: Hasan is reported to say the verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r3.anchor: وعن الحس نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r4.claim: The better-known occasion is al-As ibn Wa'il: after Khabbab ibn al-Aratt demanded payment for jewelry, al-As invoked the claimed resurrection and Paradise's gold and silver, promising to pay after receiving wealth and children there.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#3/r4.anchor: والمشهور أنها في العاص بن وائل فقد روى ان خباب بن الارت صاغ للعاص بن وائل حليا فاقتضاه الاجر

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r1.speaker: خباب
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r1.claim: Khabbāb had a debt owed by al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil; when pressed to deny Muḥammad, he refused until the debtor died and was raised, and al-ʿĀṣ mocked that he would repay when restored to wealth and children. The report is transmitted by Muslim and Bukhārī.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r1.anchor: عن خباب قال كان لي على العاص بن وائل دين فأتيته أتقاضاه

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say blacksmith Khabbāb had made jewelry for al-ʿĀṣ; al-ʿĀṣ mocked repayment in Paradise, claiming he would have wealth there and Khabbāb no greater entitlement.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل: كان خباب قينا فصاغ للعاص حليا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses looking into the unseen as looking into the Preserved Tablet.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أنظر في اللوح المحفوظ

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r5.claim: Mujāhid takes it as knowing the unseen, including whether he will be in Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أعلم الغيب حتى يعلم أفي الجنة هو أم لا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r6.speaker: قتادة والثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r6.claim: Qatāda and al-Thawrī explain the covenant as a righteous deed; other views are monotheism, a promise, or al-Kalbī’s claim that he covenanted to enter Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r6.anchor: قال قتادة والثوري: أي عملا صالحا. وقيل: هو التوحيد

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r7.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the verses were revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, but al-Qurṭubī prefers the al-ʿĀṣ report because it is recorded in the sound collections.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن: إن الآيات نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة. والأول أصح

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r6.claim: The opening alif is interrogative because “am” follows; it arose from two alifs, with the second, hamzat al-waṣl, deleted.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r6.anchor: ألفه ألف استفهام لمجيء «أم» بعدها، ومعناه التوبيخ

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r7.claim: Unlike forms such as “a-llāhu” and “a-al-dhakrayn,” this question needs no lengthening to distinguish it from a statement: the interrogative has fatḥa and declarative kasra.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r7.anchor: ولم يحتاجوا إلى هذه المدة في قوله: «أطلع» لأن ألف الاستفهام مفتوحة

RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r8.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r8.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains aṭṭalaʿa al-ghayb through ascending a mountain's summit, and says the claimed future could only be reached through unseen knowledge or a covenant with its knower.
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r8.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : أطلع الغيب من قولهم أطلع الجبل

RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r9.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r9.claim: The covenant is also explained as testimony of faith; Qatada asks whether the claimant had offered a good deed on which to base his expectation.
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r9.anchor: وقيل : في العهد كلمة الشهادة عن قتادة هل له عمل صالح قدمه

STUDYQURAN:19:77/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r5.claim: The Unseen comprises what lies beyond ordinary external human knowledge, including knowledge based on the senses and conjecture.
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r5.anchor: The Unseen refers to all that is beyond ordinary and external human means of knowing or understanding

STUDYQURAN:19:77/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r6.claim: Here the Unseen specifically means realities of the next world.
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r6.anchor: In this context, it refers specifically to the realities of the next world.

STUDYQURAN:19:77/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r7.claim: God may disclose some unseen matters to prophets or others, but alone possesses the keys of the Unseen and alone knows it.
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r7.anchor: God alone possesses the keys of the Unseen, none knows them but He (6:59)

STUDYQURAN:19:77/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r8.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r8.claim: One interpretation of the pact asks whether the disbeliever believed God, obeyed His commands, and avoided His prohibitions, thereby meriting reward in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r8.anchor: according to some, “Has he believed in God and acted upon His Commands and avoided what He has prohibited?” (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:19:77/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r9.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r9.claim: Another interpretation takes the pact to mean a promise of entry into the Garden.
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r9.anchor: “Has he made a pact that he would enter the Garden?” (Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:19:77/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r10.claim: The rhetorical questions challenge people who confidently expect bliss or escape from punishment without grounds, as in 2:80 and 53:35.
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r10.anchor: Similar rhetorical questions about possessing knowledge of the Unseen, or having a special pact or covenant with God are found in 2:80 and 53:35

NAHHAS:v3p27/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p27/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p27/r3.claim: The interrogative alif carries rebuke; the wasl alif is dropped because no longer needed.
NAHHAS:v3p27/r3.anchor: ألف الاستفهام وفيه معنى التوبيخ وحذفت ألف الوصل

TAB-FULL:v15p621/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p621/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p621/r1.claim: Al-Tabari specifies that the promised reward is wealth and children.

TAB-FULL:v15p621/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p621/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p621/r2.claim: A covenant would require evidence of prior righteous conduct.
TAB-FULL:v15p621/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا} بعمل صالح قدمه

TAB-FULL:v15p621/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p621/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p621/r3.claim: Qatāda says the covenant would be a good deed performed beforehand.
TAB-FULL:v15p621/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {أطلع الغيب أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا} بعمل صالح قدمه

TABATABAI:19:78-79/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r6.claim: The two rhetorical questions deny that the speaker knows the unseen or has a covenant with God; he has no basis for certainty that disbelief will bring the promised reward.
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r6.anchor: فليس بمطلع على الغيب حتى يعلم بأنه سيؤتى بكفره ما يأمله ولا بمتخذ عهدا عند الله حتى يطمئن إليه في ذلك

TABATABAI:19:80/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80/r4.speaker: الأكثر
TABATABAI:19:80/r4.claim: On the majority reading, the speaker is ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who swears he will receive wealth and children in Paradise after resurrection; God asks whether he knows the unseen or has a covenant, then strips him of possessions and brings him alone.
TABATABAI:19:80/r4.anchor: بناء على كونه ناظرا إلى الإيتاء في الآخرة كما اختاره الأكثر فمعنى الآيات كما فسروها تعجب من الذي كفر بآياتنا وهو عاص بن وائل أو وليد بن المغيرة

TABATABAI:19:80#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r2.claim: The reports do not fit the context: they make the saying a mockery by someone who denied resurrection, whereas the passage answers it with a serious argument.
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r2.anchor: على صراحتها في كونها كلمة استهزاء لا تنطبق على الآية

TABATABAI:19:80#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r5.claim: An argument from unseen knowledge is irrelevant to a mere taunt, since such a taunt need not depend on the speaker believing the premise he uses against an opponent.
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r5.anchor: إذ الإلزام والتبكيت لا يتوقف على العلم بصدق ما يلزم به حتى يتوقف عن منشأ علمه

TABRISI:19:78/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:78/r1.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read walad with ḍamma on wāw and sukūn on lām in four Maryam positions, al-Zukhruf, and Nūḥ, six in all.
TABRISI:19:78/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي ولدا بضم الواو وسكون اللام في هذه السورة أربعة مواضع

TABRISI:19:78/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:78/r2.claim: Basrans, Ibn Kathīr, and Khalaf use the rounded form only in Sūrat Nūḥ.
TABRISI:19:78/r2.anchor: وقرأ أهل البصرة وابن كثير وخلف في سورة نوح بالضم فقط

TABRISI:19:78/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:78/r3.claim: All remaining readers use fatḥa on both wāw and lām throughout the Qurʾān.
TABRISI:19:78/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح الواو واللام في جميع القرآن

TABRISI:19:78/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r4.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:19:78/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a Banū Asad proverb as evidence for the singular use of walad.
TABRISI:19:78/r4.anchor: قال الفراء من أمثال بني أسد

TABRISI:19:78/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r5.speaker: معاذ الخرشي
TABRISI:19:78/r5.claim: Muʿādh al-Khurashī maintains that walad is only plural and cites a poetic line that seems to use it as singular.
TABRISI:19:78/r5.anchor: وكان معاذ الخرشي يقول لا يكون الولد إلا جمعا وهذا واحد يعني الذي في المثل

TABRISI:19:78/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:19:78/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī rejects Muʿādh’s restriction: walad may be plural or singular, like other paired forms, and the cited verse proves singular use.
TABRISI:19:78/r6.anchor: يجوز أن يكون جمعا كأسد وأسد ويجوز أن يكون واحدا فيكون ولد وولد كحزن وحزن وعرب وعرب

TABRISI:19:78/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r7.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:19:78/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the poet’s phrase walad ḥimār shows singular usage, like fulk, which can be singular or plural.
TABRISI:19:78/r7.anchor: وليت فلانا كان ولد حمار يدل على أنه واحد ليس بجمع فهو مثل الفلك

TABRISI:19:78/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:78/r8.claim: In afaraʾayta, the relative clause is the first object of raʾayta and the interrogative clause aṭṭalaʿa al-ghayb is the second.
TABRISI:19:78/r8.anchor: الموصول هو المفعول الأول لرأيت والاستفهام في موضع المفعول الثاني

TABRISI:19:78/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r9.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:19:78/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats kallā as rebuke, restraint, and alert: it should stop and awaken the speaker to his error.
TABRISI:19:78/r9.anchor: كلا زجر وردع وتنبيه أي هذا مما يرتدع به وينبه على وجه الضلالة فيه

TABRISI:19:78/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r10.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:19:78/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows kallā to connect with what follows, as in kallā wa-rabbi al-kaʿbah.
TABRISI:19:78/r10.anchor: يكون صلة لما بعدها كقولك كلا ورب الكعبة

TABRISI:19:78/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r11.speaker: أبو حاتم
TABRISI:19:78/r11.claim: Abū Ḥātim says Qurʾānic kallā has two senses, negation and an attention marker akin to illā, with some contexts admitting both readings.
TABRISI:19:78/r11.anchor: جاءت في القرآن على وجهين بمعنى لا يكون ذلك وبمعنى إلا التي للتنبيه

TABRISI:19:78/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r12.speaker: أبو حاتم
TABRISI:19:78/r12.claim: Abū Ḥātim says both senses can apply in some places and notes that kallā can also begin a fresh statement, as in al-ʿAlaq 96:6.
TABRISI:19:78/r12.anchor: وجاءت في مواضع متوجهة على التأويلين ويدل على ذلك أنها قد تكون مبتدأة

TABRISI:19:78/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r13.speaker: الأعشى
TABRISI:19:78/r13.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s verse uses kallā in a rebuking response before continuing the assertion.
TABRISI:19:78/r13.anchor: كلا زعمتم بأنا لا نقاتلكم إنا لأمثالكم يا قومنا قتل

TABRISI:19:78/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r14.speaker: أبو العباس
TABRISI:19:78/r14.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās says one should not pause at kallā because it is an answer whose point comes in what follows.
TABRISI:19:78/r14.anchor: لا يوقف على كلا لأنها جواب والفائدة تقع فيما بعدها

TABRISI:19:78/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:78/r15.claim: Another view permits pausing at kallā; the source notes that stopping on it is among the Qurʾān’s difficult pause questions.
TABRISI:19:78/r15.anchor: وقيل: يجوز الوقف عليه. ومن مشكلات الوقف في القرآن

TABRISI:19:78/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:78/r16.claim: The author classifies ten kallā locations as good both for pausing and restarting when kallā rejects what came before; if it means an alert or affirmation, one restarts there.
TABRISI:19:78/r16.anchor: أحدها: ما يحسن الوقف عليه ويحسن الابتداء به

TABRISI:19:78/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:78/r17.claim: The first-category examples include the covenant and idol-honor passages, plus examples about return, partners, escape, gardens, increase, scripture, divine dishonor, and wealth preserving life.
TABRISI:19:78/r17.anchor: أم اتخذوا عند الرحمان عهدا كلا

TABRISI:19:78/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:78/r18.claim: These examples can take either analysis: kallā rejects the preceding statement, or it begins a new alert or emphatic statement.
TABRISI:19:78/r18.anchor: فمن جعل كلا في هذه المواضع ردا للأول بمعنى لا ليس الأمر كذلك وقف عليه

TABRISI:19:78-82/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78-82/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:19:78-82/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid take the question as asking whether the man knows the unseen well enough to know if he is destined for Paradise.
TABRISI:19:78-82/r5.anchor: أعلم الغيب حتى يعلم أهو في الجنة أم لا عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

TABRISI:19:78-82/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78-82/r6.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:19:78-82/r6.claim: Al-Kalbī says the man claims to have looked into the Preserved Tablet and learned that wealth and children will be granted him.
TABRISI:19:78-82/r6.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنظر في اللوح المحفوظ عن الكلبي وتأويله أشرف على علم الغيب

TABRISI:19:78-82/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78-82/r7.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:19:78-82/r7.claim: Qatāda explains the covenant as a good deed the man previously offered to God.
TABRISI:19:78-82/r7.anchor: اتخذ عند الله عهدا بعمل صالح قدمه عن قتادة

TABRISI:19:78-82/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78-82/r8.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:19:78-82/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī takes the covenant to mean that God promised the man admission to Paradise.
TABRISI:19:78-82/r8.anchor: وقيل: معناه أم عهد الله إليه أنه يدخل الجنة عن الكلبي

TABRISI:19:78-82/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78-82/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:19:78-82/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the covenant is confession of God’s oneness, through which God may show mercy.
TABRISI:19:78-82/r9.anchor: وقيل: معناه أم قال لا إله إلا الله فيرحمه الله بها عن ابن عباس

THALABI:v6p229/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p229/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p229/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas takes “has he seen the unseen?” to ask whether the man looked into the Preserved Tablet.
THALABI:v6p229/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أنظر في اللوح المحفوظ

THALABI:v6p229/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p229/r4.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p229/r4.claim: Mujahid takes it to ask whether he knows the unseen, including whether he will be in Paradise.
THALABI:v6p229/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أعلم علم الغيب حتى يعلم أفي الجنة هو أم لا

THALABI:v6p229/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p229/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p229/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the covenant with the Merciful as professing that there is no god but God.
THALABI:v6p229/r5.anchor: يعني أم قال: لا إله إلا الله

THALABI:v6p229/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p229/r6.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p229/r6.claim: Qatada explains the covenant as a good deed already performed.
THALABI:v6p229/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: يعني عملا صالحا قدمه

THALABI:v6p229/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p229/r7.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v6p229/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says the covenant is God’s assurance that He will admit the man to Paradise.
THALABI:v6p229/r7.anchor: وقال الكلبي: عهد إليه أنه يدخله الجنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r1.claim: Did he see the unseen? means, does he know whether he will be in Paradise?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس، ومجاهد: (يريد أعلم ما غاب عنه حتى يعلم أفي الجنة هو أم لا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r2.claim: The question means: look into the Preserved Tablet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (معناه: انظر في اللوح المحفوظ)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r3.claim: A covenant with the Merciful means saying there is no god but God and thereby seeking mercy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: من قال: لا إله إلا الله فارحمه بها)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r4.claim: The covenant may mean having done a good deed and therefore hoping for reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: (يعني: أقدم عملا صالحا فهو يرجوه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r5.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r5.claim: The covenant means obedience to God.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r6.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r6.claim: A report says one who performs the prescribed prayers on time without neglect has God’s covenant to enter Paradise, while one who neglects them has no covenant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r6.anchor: وهذا القول منتزع مما روى أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- قال: "يقول الله: من صلى الصلوات لوقتها ولم يذرها استخفافا بها لقيني يوم القيامة وله عندي عهدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r7.claim: On that interpretation, the verse asks whether he performed the five prayers and thereby took a covenant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r7.anchor: وعلى [هذا المعنى فالآية] (¬5): أم صلى الصلوات الخمس فاتخذ بها عندي عهدا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r8.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r8.claim: The covenant may mean that God promised him admission to Paradise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (أعهد إليه الله أنه يدخله الجنة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r9.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj selects the interpretation that the person received a covenant from God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p312/r9.anchor: وهو اختيار الزجاج يقول: (أم أعطى عهدا)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:76-78/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:76-78/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:76-78/r4.claim: The challenge asks whether he knows the unseen well enough to know he will enter Paradise or has a covenant with God; the covenant would be professing that there is no god but God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:76-78/r4.anchor: أطلع الغيب } أعلم علم الغيب حتى عرف أنه في الجنة { أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا } أم قال: لا إله إلا الله حتى يستحق دخول الجنة؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r4.claim: The question asks whether he has seen the Unseen and learned its contents; the answer is that he has not.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r4.anchor: على الاستفهام، فعلم ما فيه، أي لم يطلع على الغيب

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r5.claim: The claimant has not made a covenant with the Merciful; its explanation follows later in the verse.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r5.anchor: أي لم يفعل، وتفسيره في آخر هذه الآية

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r6.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r6.claim: Khabbāb reports that al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil withheld his wages unless he disavowed Muhammad, then promised to repay after resurrection from future wealth and children; Khabbāb told the Prophet, and these verses were revealed.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r6.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال: كنت قينا في الجاهلية فعملت للعاصي بن وائل حتى اجتمعت لي عنده دراهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r7.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r7.claim: Qatāda reports that a Companion seeking a debt from a polytheist heard the debtor promise repayment in Paradise, claiming he would have wealth and children there; the challenge asks if he had seen the Unseen.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r7.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: ذكر لنا أن رجلا من أصحاب النبي عليه السلام أتى رجلا من المشركين

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r1.claim: The covenant with the Merciful means performing a righteous deed.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r1.anchor: {أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا} [مريم: 78] بعمل صالح.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r2.claim: The Prophet says that one who performs the five prayers completely has God's covenant to enter Paradise; one who does not may be punished or forgiven.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r2.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «خمس صلوات كتبهن الله على عباده من جاء بهن تامات

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r3.claim: Qatāda also interprets the covenant as a righteous deed.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r3.anchor: وقد قال سعيد، عن قتادة قال: {أم اتخذ عند الرحمن عهدا} [مريم: 78] بعمل صالح.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r4.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p242/r4.claim: Some identify the covenant as monotheism.

SAMIN-DURR:19:78/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:78/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:78/r1.claim: The interrogative hamza causes hamzat al-waṣl to drop; another reading omits the question hamza in connected speech and uses kasra initially, as a poem shows.
SAMIN-DURR:19:78/r1.anchor: قوله: { أطلع }: هذه همزة استفهام سقط من أجلها همزة الوصل.

SAMIN-DURR:19:78/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:78/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:78/r2.claim: اطلع means climb to a mountain's summit; Jarir's line uses مطلع in this sense.
SAMIN-DURR:19:78/r2.anchor: واطلع من قولهم: اطلع فلان الجبل، أي: ارتقى أعلاه. قال جرير:

SAMIN-DURR:19:78/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:78/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:78/r3.claim: الغيب is a direct object, not one governed by a deleted preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:19:78/r3.anchor: ف " الغيب " ، مفعول به، لا على إسقاط حرف الجر،

ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r7.claim: The question asks whether the boastful man has seen the unseen or received a covenant from the Merciful; it echoes the claim that he would receive something better if returned to God.
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r7.anchor: أي علم ذلك غيبا أم أعطي عهدا

ASAD-NOTES:19:77#n67/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:77#n67/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:77#n67/r1.claim: Al-ghayb here means the unknowable future.
ASAD-NOTES:19:77#n67/r1.anchor: In this context, the term al-ghayb denotes the unknowable future

BURHAN:v4p313/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p313/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p313/r1.claim: كلا is the opposite of affirmative إي when used as a rejection, as in the response to the boast that the unbeliever has access to the unseen or a covenant.

BURHAN:v4p313/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p313/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p313/r2.claim: In other settings كلا can mean حقا and serve as an oath adjunct, as in كلا والقمر; it may also introduce confirmations about judgment and the records of deeds.

BURHAN:v4p313/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p313/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p313/r3.claim: The كلا after the claim that wealth made its owner immortal can mean either a rebuke or an affirmation.

BURHAN:v4p313/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p313/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p313/r4.claim: Readers differ over pausing around كلا: some pause on it as rebuke, others begin with it as confirmation; the author prefers pausing when it rebukes and beginning with it when it confirms.
BURHAN:v4p313/r4.anchor: ومنهم من نظر إلى المعنيين فيقف عليها إذا كانت بمعنى الردع

BURHAN:v4p313/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p313/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v4p313/r5.claim: Some interpret ذلك and هذا as opposites of negation, and كذلك as an opposite of كلا, meaning ‘that is how it was done’; the author cites the following conjunction as evidence of an implied preceding clause.

BURHAN:v4p313/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p313/r6.speaker: الخليل
BURHAN:v4p313/r6.claim: Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, al-Akhfash, al-Mubarrad, and al-Zajjaj explain كلا meaning لا as rejecting an elided clause, approximately ليس الأمر كذلك; it is used at a pause for rebuke, denial, or rejection.

BURHAN:v4p313/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p313/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p313/r7.claim: Because كلا carries threat and warning, it appears only in Meccan suras; the author says a sura containing it should therefore be recognized as Meccan.
BURHAN:v4p313/r7.anchor: ولذلك لم تقع في القرآن إلا في سورة مكية

BURHAN:v1p368/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p368/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p368/r1.claim: The first class of Qur’anic كلا permits both pausing before it and beginning after it, depending on whether it is read as rebuke or confirmation; twelve examples are listed, including these four.
BURHAN:v1p368/r1.anchor: إحداها ما يجوز الوقف عليه والابتداء به

ITQAN:v1p234/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p234/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p234/r9.claim: Kallā occurs thirty-three times; seven are unanimously rebukes at which pausing is permitted, including the examples listed.
ITQAN:v1p234/r9.anchor: كلا في القرآن في ثلاثة وثلاثين موضعا منها سبعة للردع إتفاقا فيوقف عليها وذلك

DAMGHANI:v1p344/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p344/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p344/r12.claim: In the question about having looked into the unseen, al-ghayb means the Preserved Tablet.
DAMGHANI:v1p344/r12.anchor: الغيب اللوح المحفوظ قوله تعالى في سورة مريم اطلع الغيب

DAMGHANI:v1p344/r24.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p344/r24.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p344/r24.claim: The entry begins its list of senses for fitnah by glossing it as associationism, but the excerpt cuts off before its example.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p456/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p456/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p456/r1.claim: Al-ghayb is what is hidden from you; the related forms also describe the sun setting, a woman whose husband is away, a depression in the land, and a thicket.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p456/r1.anchor: الغيب : ما غاب عنك . يقال : غابت الشمس مغيبا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p456/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p456/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p456/r8.claim: A seventh sense is the Preserved Tablet, also asked about in the verse from al-Ṭūr.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p456/r8.anchor: والسابع : اللوح المحفوظ . ومنه قوله تعالى في مريم :

BUKHARI:2091/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:2091/r1.speaker: خباب
BUKHARI:2091/r1.claim: Khabbab reports that al-As ibn Wa'il withheld his debt until he disbelieved, then claimed he would regain wealth and children after resurrection; the revelation rebuts that claim.
BUKHARI:2091/r1.anchor: عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، عَنْ خَبَّابٍ، قَالَ كُنْتُ قَيْنًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، وَكَانَ لِي عَلَى الْعَاصِ بْنِ وَائِلٍ دَيْنٌ

BUKHARI:4733/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4733/r1.speaker: خباب
BUKHARI:4733/r1.claim: Khabbab reports that al-As ibn Wa'il refused payment unless he disbelieved, then asserted he would have wealth and children after resurrection; the verses expose this claim as baseless.
BUKHARI:4733/r1.anchor: عَنْ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ أَبِي الضُّحَى، عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، عَنْ خَبَّابٍ، قَالَ كُنْتُ قَيْنًا بِمَكَّةَ،

BUKHARI:4733/r2.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4733/r2.speaker: author
BUKHARI:4733/r2.claim: The report adds a gloss to the alleged covenant, construing it as a binding pledge or guarantee.
BUKHARI:4733/r2.anchor: قَالَ مَوْثِقًا‏.‏ لَمْ يَقُلِ الأَشْجَعِيُّ عَنْ سُفْيَانَ سَيْفًا

BUKHARI:4735/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4735/r1.speaker: خباب
BUKHARI:4735/r1.claim: Khabbab reports that al-As ibn Wa'il promised to pay his debt from wealth and children after resurrection; the passage was revealed to reject that boast and foretell punishment and his solitary return to God.
BUKHARI:4735/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي الضُّحَى، عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، عَنْ خَبَّابٍ، قَالَ كُنْتُ رَجُلًا قَيِّنًا، وَكَانَ لِي عَلَى الْعَاصِي بْنِ وَائِلٍ دَيْنٌ

MUSNAD-AHMAD:21076/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21076/r1.speaker: خباب
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21076/r1.claim: Khabbab reports that al-As ibn Wa'il refused to repay him unless he renounced Muhammad, then boasted of future wealth and children; God revealed 19:77–78 challenging his claim to unseen knowledge or a divine pledge.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21076/r1.anchor: عن خباب، قال: " كنت رجلا قينا، وكان لي على العاص بن وائل حق، فأتيته أتقاضاه
